h1: AWS IAM policy best practices: least privilege without the pain
html:
Home/Insights/Cloud
CLOUD

AWS IAM policy best practices: least privilege without the pain

How to write secure AWS IAM policies: least privilege, roles instead of access keys, permission boundaries, SCPs, conditions and IAM Access Analyzer.

By VISIBI Cloud team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·11 min read
QUICK ANSWER

How to write secure AWS IAM policies: least privilege, roles instead of access keys, permission boundaries, SCPs, conditions and IAM Access Analyzer.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Use IAM roles and temporary credentials — avoid long-lived access keys.
✓Start from AWS managed policies, then tighten with IAM Access Analyzer.
✓Use AWS Organizations SCPs as guardrails across all accounts.
✓Protect the root user with MFA and never use it day-to-day.

How IAM policies are evaluated

An IAM request is allowed only if an identity or resource policy explicitly allows it and nothing explicitly denies it. Explicit deny always wins. Service control policies (SCPs) and permission boundaries set the maximum permissions — they never grant access on their own.

RELATED GUIDE12 proven ways to reduce your AWS bill →

1. Prefer roles and short-lived credentials

Give people access through IAM Identity Center (single sign-on) and give workloads IAM roles (EC2 instance profiles, ECS task roles, Lambda execution roles). Temporary credentials expire automatically, so leaked keys are far less dangerous.

2. Apply least privilege

  • Start with AWS managed job-function policies, then narrow down
  • Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate policies from CloudTrail activity
  • Scope Resource to specific ARNs instead of "*"
  • Review “last accessed” data and remove unused permissions
Want an AWS security review?Certified AWS architects review your IAM, network and logging against the Well-Architected Framework.Book a free AWS consultation →

3. Use conditions

Conditions make policies much safer. Common examples: require MFA (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent), restrict by source VPC or IP (aws:SourceVpc, aws:SourceIp), enforce tags (aws:ResourceTag) and limit regions (aws:RequestedRegion).

4. Guardrails with SCPs and permission boundaries

In AWS Organizations, SCPs stop anyone — even administrators — from doing things like disabling CloudTrail, leaving the organisation or using unapproved regions. Permission boundaries let developers create roles without being able to escalate their own privileges.

5. Monitor and audit

  • Enable CloudTrail in every account and region
  • Turn on IAM Access Analyzer for external and unused access
  • Use AWS Config rules and Security Hub for IAM checks
  • Manage IAM in Terraform so every change is reviewed

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Buying commitments before rightsizing
✕No tagging, so nobody knows who owns the spend
✕Click-ops changes that can’t be reproduced or audited
✕Migrating without a rollback plan
HOW VISIBI CAN HELP

How we help with cloud

01AssessCertified architects review cost, security and reliability.
02PlanA prioritised roadmap with savings and risks quantified.
03ImplementChanges delivered as Terraform with zero-downtime rollout.
04OperateFinOps reviews, monitoring and optional 24/7 managed services.

Frequently asked questions

What is least privilege in AWS?

Granting only the permissions needed for a task, on only the resources needed, for only as long as needed.

Should I use IAM users?

For people, AWS recommends IAM Identity Center instead of IAM users. For workloads, use roles.

What is the difference between an SCP and an IAM policy?

An SCP sets the maximum permissions for accounts in an organisation; IAM policies grant permissions within that limit.

h1: Is Cloudflare worth it? 9 benefits for ecommerce and business websites
html:
Home/Insights/Performance
PERFORMANCE

Is Cloudflare worth it? 9 benefits for ecommerce and business websites

Faster pages, DDoS protection, a WAF, bot management and lower hosting costs — the real benefits of Cloudflare and when it’s worth paying for Pro or Business.

By VISIBI Hosting team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·8 min read
QUICK ANSWER

Faster pages, DDoS protection, a WAF, bot management and lower hosting costs — the real benefits of Cloudflare and when it’s worth paying for Pro or Business.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Cloudflare sits between visitors and your server — caching, securing and accelerating traffic.
✓The free plan covers CDN, SSL and basic DDoS protection.
✓Pro and Business add a managed WAF, image optimisation and better bot controls.
✓Offloading traffic to the edge can reduce hosting costs as well as speeding sites up.

What Cloudflare actually does

Cloudflare is a reverse proxy and global edge network. When you point your DNS at Cloudflare, visitors connect to the nearest Cloudflare data centre instead of your server. Cloudflare serves cached content directly and forwards the rest — filtering attacks along the way.

RELATED GUIDEHow to reduce CLS in Google PageSpeed Insights (with fixes that work) →

The 9 biggest benefits

  • Speed: static files (and optionally HTML) served from the edge close to each visitor
  • DDoS protection: unmetered network-layer protection on every plan
  • Web Application Firewall: managed rules block SQL injection, XSS and known exploits (Pro and above)
  • Bot management: challenge scrapers, credential stuffing and card-testing bots
  • Free SSL and automatic HTTPS
  • Image optimisation: Polish and Mirage (Pro) compress and resize images
  • Lower hosting costs: fewer requests reach your origin, so smaller servers cope
  • Better uptime: “Always Online” can serve cached pages if your server fails
  • Rules and Workers: redirects, headers and edge logic without touching your app
Want Cloudflare set up properly?We configure and tune Cloudflare for Magento, WooCommerce and WordPress with zero downtime.Get a free WAF review →

Free vs Pro vs Business

For a brochure site the free plan is often enough. Online stores usually benefit from Pro for the managed WAF and image optimisation. Business adds a 100% uptime SLA, more WAF rules and PCI-oriented features, which suits high-revenue stores.

Cloudflare for Magento, WooCommerce and Shopify

Magento and WooCommerce benefit most, because they are self-hosted: Cloudflare can cache static assets, protect admin URLs and absorb bot traffic. Shopify already runs on its own CDN, so Cloudflare is mainly useful there for DNS and email security. Be careful caching HTML for logged-in customers or carts — use cache rules that bypass cookies such as PHPSESSID or woocommerce_items_in_cart.

Common mistakes

  • Caching pages with personal data (carts, account pages)
  • Leaving the origin IP exposed so attackers bypass Cloudflare
  • Turning on every security feature at once and blocking real customers
  • Forgetting to allow payment gateway callbacks and webhooks

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Only testing the homepage
✕Optimising lab scores instead of real-user data
✕Adding third-party scripts without a performance budget
✕Leaving load testing until the week before peak

Yes, there is a generous free plan. Paid plans add a managed WAF, image optimisation, more rules and support.

Usually yes, especially for visitors far from your server, because cached content is served from the nearest edge location.

Is Cloudflare good for Magento?

Yes — it is a popular choice for Magento Open Source, alongside or instead of Varnish, as long as cache rules respect customer sessions.

h1: Black Friday load testing: how to make sure your store stays online

Home/Insights/Performance
PERFORMANCE

Black Friday load testing: how to make sure your store stays online

How to load test an ecommerce store before Black Friday: realistic scenarios, target numbers, tools, what to fix and how to run a peak-day war room.

By VISIBI Hosting team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·9 min read
QUICK ANSWER

How to load test an ecommerce store before Black Friday: realistic scenarios, target numbers, tools, what to fix and how to run a peak-day war room.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Test real journeys — search, filter, basket, checkout — not just the homepage.
✓Aim for 2–3× last year’s peak traffic.
✓Databases, search and checkout usually fail before web servers.
✓Finish testing and fixes before your code freeze.

Set your targets

Take last year’s busiest hour from analytics — sessions per minute, orders per minute and page views per session — then plan for 2–3× that to cover growth and marketing spikes.

RELATED GUIDEIs Cloudflare worth it? 9 benefits for ecommerce and business websites →

Build realistic scenarios

  • Browsers: homepage → category → filters → product
  • Searchers: site search and layered navigation
  • Buyers: add to basket → checkout → payment (use a test gateway)
  • Logged-in customers with accounts and wishlists
  • Background: bots, APIs and integrations
Will your store survive Black Friday?Free peak-readiness audit from engineers who have kept stores online for 20 years.Book a free audit →

Tools

k6, JMeter, Gatling, Locust and cloud services like BlazeMeter or Grafana Cloud k6 can all generate peak load. Run tests from outside your network against a production-like environment, and monitor with New Relic, Datadog or CloudWatch while they run.

What usually breaks — and the fix

  • Database: slow queries on filters and search — add indexes, use OpenSearch/Elasticsearch
  • Cache: full-page cache bypassed by cookies — fix hole-punching
  • Sessions: file sessions locking — move to Redis
  • Autoscaling: scales too slowly — pre-warm capacity for peak
  • Third parties: slow scripts and APIs — add timeouts and async loading

Run a war room

On peak days, have engineers watching live dashboards with a clear runbook: who can scale, roll back, switch off heavy features or enable a queue page. Agree it before the day.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Only testing the homepage
✕Optimising lab scores instead of real-user data
✕Adding third-party scripts without a performance budget
✕Leaving load testing until the week before peak

h1: 12 category page techniques that increase ecommerce conversion
html:
Home/Insights/Ecommerce
ECOMMERCE

12 category page techniques that increase ecommerce conversion

Proven ways to make ecommerce category pages convert: filters, sorting, product cards, merchandising, speed, mobile UX and SEO content.

By VISIBI CRO team·Reviewed by Adnan Khan, Co-founder & CEO·Updated 29 September 2026·10 min read
QUICK ANSWER

Proven ways to make ecommerce category pages convert: filters, sorting, product cards, merchandising, speed, mobile UX and SEO content.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Category pages are where most shoppers decide what to click — treat them as a key conversion page.
✓Good filters and sorting matter more than clever design.
✓Product cards need price, key specs, reviews and stock at a glance.
✓Speed and mobile layout directly affect browse-to-product rate.

Help shoppers find the right product

  • Show the filters people actually use first (size, price, brand, rating) — check site search and analytics
  • Show product counts on filter options and hide options with zero results
  • Keep filters visible on desktop and in a sticky button on mobile
  • Offer useful sorts: best sellers, top rated, price, newest
  • Use applied-filter chips that are easy to remove
RELATED GUIDEGoogle Merchant Center feed optimisation: fix disapprovals and win more Shopping clicks →

Make product cards do more work

  • Clear price, including savings against RRP
  • Star rating with review count
  • Two or three key attributes (e.g. firmness, size)
  • Stock and delivery messages (“In stock – next-day delivery”)
  • Colour swatches that switch the image
  • Quick add-to-basket for simple products
Want more sales from the same traffic?Our CRO team researches, tests and ships category page improvements.Get a free CRO audit →

Merchandise deliberately

Pin best-sellers and high-margin products near the top, promote new ranges, and push out-of-stock items to the end. Add banners sparingly — one relevant banner between rows converts better than a carousel above the grid.

Speed and mobile

Category pages carry many images, so lazy-load below the fold, serve modern formats (WebP/AVIF) and reserve image space to avoid layout shift. On mobile, two products per row with large tap targets usually outperforms one per row.

SEO without hurting conversion

Put a short intro above the grid and longer buying-guide content below it. Use canonical tags and noindex rules to stop filter combinations creating thousands of thin pages, and add FAQ content to earn AI and rich-result visibility.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Choosing a platform on licence price instead of total cost of ownership
✕Launching a new site without an SEO redirect plan
✕Adding extensions and apps without checking performance or security
✕Leaving upgrades until peak season

Infinite scroll or pagination?

A “load more” button is usually the best balance: easy to browse, keeps the footer reachable and is SEO-friendly with crawlable paginated URLs.

How many products per page?

24–48 on desktop is typical; test against your catalogue and speed.

Should category pages have text?

Yes — a short intro and helpful content below the products help SEO without pushing products down.

Crawler and bot traffic causing Magento performance incidents

Aggressive crawlers hitting uncached filter and search URLs can overload Magento. Combine Fastly/WAF rules, caching and app fixes to stop it.

Aggressive crawlers hitting uncached filter and search URLs can overload Magento. Combine Fastly/WAF rules, caching and app fixes to stop it.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

Automated crawler traffic on expensive, uncached URLs created substantial application and database load until edge rules and caching were tightened.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Bots often hit expensive, uncached URLs like layered navigation and search.
✓Rate limiting and bot rules at the edge protect origin capacity.
✓Don’t block good bots like Googlebot.

Why bots hurt

A single aggressive crawler requesting thousands of filter combinations can generate more database load than real shoppers.

  • Block known bad ASNs
  • Monitor top user agents and IPs

✕Waiting until after a breach to act
✕Restoring a backup without fixing the entry point
✕Leaving old plugins, extensions and admin users in place
✕Relying on a single tool instead of layered defences

Old code isn’t automatically bad. How to make evidence-led technical debt decisions — and when stability beats architectural purity.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

A broad service-layer migration of a catalogue integration would have added more risk than benefit. The legacy code was outdated but stable, so we documented and monitored it instead.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Working, production-critical code carries low risk while untouched.
✓Refactor when there is a measurable business benefit or real risk.
✓Wrap and monitor legacy code instead of rewriting it blindly.
AT A GLANCE
How we score whether to refactor
Security riskRefactor
Blocks upgradeRefactor

The rewrite trap

Rewrites feel productive but often reintroduce old bugs and new behaviour differences — especially in stock, pricing and order integrations.

If it works, is monitored and doesn’t block anything, document it and add tests instead.

Don’t store runtime timestamps in Magento configuration

Writing heartbeat timestamps or runtime state into Magento configuration invalidates config cache and causes unnecessary churn. Use flags or a dedicated table instead.

QUICK ANSWER

Writing heartbeat timestamps or runtime state into Magento configuration invalidates config cache and causes unnecessary churn. Use flags or a dedicated table instead.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

A custom integration saved heartbeat timestamps into Magento configuration. Moving that runtime state into Magento flags stopped needless configuration cache invalidations.

KEY TAKEAWAYS

Some integrations save “last run” timestamps into core_config_data on every run. Each save can trigger config cache invalidation, forcing Magento to rebuild configuration and adding avoidable load.

GA4 ecommerce events: the complete setup guide

Every GA4 recommended ecommerce event explained — view_item to purchase — with the parameters you need, dataLayer examples and how to test them.

By VISIBI Analytics team·Reviewed by Adnan Khan, Co-founder & CEO·Updated 29 September 2026·10 min read
QUICK ANSWER

Every GA4 recommended ecommerce event explained — view_item to purchase — with the parameters you need, dataLayer examples and how to test them.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓GA4 uses recommended events such as view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase.
✓Each event needs an items array with item_id or item_name.
✓Send purchase once per order with a unique transaction_id to avoid duplicates.
✓Test in DebugView before trusting reports.

The recommended ecommerce events

  • view_item_list / select_item — product listings and clicks
  • view_item — product detail page
  • add_to_cart / remove_from_cart
  • view_cart
  • begin_checkout
  • add_shipping_info / add_payment_info
  • purchase — order confirmation
  • refund — full or partial refunds
  • view_promotion / select_promotion — internal banners
RELATED GUIDEMeta Conversions API explained: why your pixel isn’t enough →

Required parameters

Every ecommerce event should include currency, value and an items array. Each item needs item_id or item_name, plus price and quantity. Add item_brand, item_category (up to five levels), item_variant and coupon for richer reports. The purchase event also needs transaction_id, and ideally tax and shipping.

Is your GA4 tracking accurate?We set up GA4, GTM and ad conversions properly — tested against real orders.Get a free tracking audit →

gtag.js or Google Tag Manager?

Both work. gtag.js is simpler for a single destination. Google Tag Manager is better when you also need Google Ads, Meta, TikTok or Microsoft Ads tags, because one dataLayer can feed them all. Platforms like Shopify now use Customer Events; Magento and WooCommerce usually need a dataLayer module or custom code.

Common mistakes

  • Firing purchase on page refresh — deduplicate with transaction_id
  • Sending value as a string with a currency symbol
  • Missing currency (revenue shows as zero)
  • Different item_id formats across events
  • Consent Mode not configured for UK/EEA traffic

How to test

Enable debug mode with the GA Debugger extension or Tag Assistant, then watch events arrive in Admin → DebugView. Place a real test order and compare GA4 revenue against your platform the next day.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Trusting GA4 numbers without checking them against real orders
✕Firing purchase events more than once per order
✕Skipping Consent Mode for UK/EEA traffic
✕Having no documentation of what is tracked and why

Consent refusals, ad blockers, missing purchase events on some payment methods and duplicate or missing transaction IDs are the usual causes.

Optimise titles first

h1: How to reduce CLS in Google PageSpeed Insights (with fixes that work)
html:
Home/Insights/Performance
PERFORMANCE

How to reduce CLS in Google PageSpeed Insights (with fixes that work)

A practical guide to Cumulative Layout Shift: what causes it, how to find the elements shifting, and proven fixes for images, fonts, banners and ecommerce pages.

By VISIBI Front-end team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·10 min read
QUICK ANSWER

A practical guide to Cumulative Layout Shift: what causes it, how to find the elements shifting, and proven fixes for images, fonts, banners and ecommerce pages.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓CLS measures unexpected layout movement; “good” is 0.1 or less at the 75th percentile.
✓Images and embeds without dimensions are the most common cause.
✓Late-loading banners, cookie bars and web fonts cause many of the rest.
✓Field data (real users) is what Google uses for rankings — lab scores are only a guide.

What CLS is and why it matters

Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) is one of Google’s three Core Web Vitals. It measures how much visible content moves unexpectedly while a page loads and during its life. A CLS of 0.1 or less is “good”; above 0.25 is “poor”. Layout shift is frustrating — customers tap the wrong button or lose their place — so it affects conversion as well as SEO.

RELATED GUIDEIs Cloudflare worth it? 9 benefits for ecommerce and business websites →

How to find what is shifting

  • Run PageSpeed Insights and open “Avoid large layout shifts” to see the elements responsible
  • In Chrome DevTools, open Performance, record a load and look for “Layout Shift” entries
  • Enable Rendering → “Layout Shift Regions” to highlight shifts in blue
  • Check the Core Web Vitals report in Search Console for affected URL groups

Fix 1: Always reserve space for images and video

Add width and height attributes (or CSS aspect-ratio) to every image, iframe and video so the browser reserves space before it loads. This matters most for product grids, hero banners and sliders.

Still failing Core Web Vitals?Our developers fix CLS, LCP and INP in code — not just in a report.Get a free SEO audit →

Fix 2: Stop banners and pop-ups pushing content down

Cookie banners, promo bars and “free delivery” strips injected after load are a classic cause. Reserve their space in the initial HTML, or overlay them with position: fixed so they don’t move content.

Fix 3: Load fonts without jumps

Web fonts can change text size when they swap in. Preload key fonts, use font-display: optional or swap, and use size-adjust / ascent-override on the fallback font so both take up the same space.

Fix 4: Ecommerce-specific fixes

  • Give product-image galleries a fixed aspect ratio
  • Reserve space for reviews widgets, “recently viewed” and recommendations
  • Avoid inserting price or stock messages above the add-to-basket button after load
  • On Magento, Hyvä themes avoid much of the layout shift common in Luma
  • Use transform animations instead of changing top/height

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Only testing the homepage
✕Optimising lab scores instead of real-user data
✕Adding third-party scripts without a performance budget
✕Leaving load testing until the week before peak

What is a good CLS score?

0.1 or less for at least 75% of page visits, measured from real users.

Why does PageSpeed show a different CLS from Search Console?

PageSpeed’s lab test measures one load; Search Console uses 28 days of real-user field data, which includes shifts after load.

Does CLS affect rankings?

Core Web Vitals are part of Google’s page experience signals. They are a tie-breaker rather than a major factor, but they also affect conversion.

Older integrations often write inventory directly. Migrating blindly to newer APIs can change behaviour — understand and test existing stock semantics first.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

A legacy integration wrote inventory directly. Before touching it, we documented its exact stock behaviour so any move to newer APIs wouldn’t silently change availability rules.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Direct writes are fast but bypass validation, events and indexing.

Many integrations were written for speed or before Multi-Source Inventory. They work, but skip Magento’s events and validation.

Capture current behaviour with test cases, migrate in a staging environment, compare results SKU by SKU and roll out gradually.

✕Starting to build before requirements and success metrics are clear
✕Not owning your code, repositories and accounts
✕Skipping automated tests to save time

Home/Insights/Security
SECURITY

Magecart and card skimming: how to protect your checkout

How Magecart-style skimmers steal card data from checkout pages, how to detect them, and the controls that stop them — including PCI DSS 4.0 script requirements.

By VISIBI Security team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·8 min read
QUICK ANSWER

How Magecart-style skimmers steal card data from checkout pages, how to detect them, and the controls that stop them — including PCI DSS 4.0 script requirements.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Skimmers inject JavaScript that copies card details as customers type.
✓Outdated platforms and third-party scripts are the most common entry points.
✓Content Security Policy, script integrity and monitoring are key defences.
BY THE NUMBERS
Layers that stop skimmers
Patchclose known vulnerabilities
CSP + SRIblock unapproved scripts
Monitordetect script changes fast

How skimming works

Attackers inject malicious JavaScript into checkout — directly on your server or via a compromised third-party script. The script silently sends card details to the attacker while the order completes normally.

RELATED GUIDEHow to stop spam and bot attacks on Adobe Commerce Cloud → Harden your Magento storeSecurity audits, patching and PCI-DSS 4.0 script controls.Get a free security audit →

Warning signs

  • Customers reporting fraud after buying from you
  • Unknown scripts or domains loading on checkout
  • Unexpected file changes
  • New admin users you don’t recognise
  • Alerts from your payment provider

Defences

  • Keep Magento / Adobe Commerce fully patched
  • Content Security Policy restricting script sources
  • Subresource Integrity for third-party scripts
  • File integrity and script change monitoring
  • Admin 2FA and restricted admin URL
  • Hosted payment fields where possible

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Waiting until after a breach to act
✕Restoring a backup without fixing the entry point
✕Leaving old plugins, extensions and admin users in place
✕Relying on a single tool instead of layered defences
HOW VISIBI CAN HELP

Frequently asked questions

Am I protected if I use a hosted payment page?

It reduces risk, but skimmers can still target pages before the redirect or fake payment forms.

h1: Magento checkout CSP problems with AJAX content (and inline JavaScript)
html:
Home/Insights/Security
SECURITY

Magento checkout CSP problems with AJAX content (and inline JavaScript)

AJAX-injected checkout HTML with inline scripts can violate Content Security Policy even when the page is compliant. Return data or markup and initialise JavaScript from modules.

By VISIBI Security team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·8 min read
QUICK ANSWER

AJAX-injected checkout HTML with inline scripts can violate Content Security Policy even when the page is compliant. Return data or markup and initialise JavaScript from modules.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

A checkout step loaded HTML via AJAX that included inline JavaScript, breaking CSP even though the parent page was compliant. We changed it to return markup and initialise the behaviour from an external module.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Stricter CSP blocks inline scripts inserted by custom and third-party modules.
✓AJAX responses containing script tags are a common hidden violation.
✓Move logic into RequireJS/AMD modules and return markup or JSON.

Why this matters now

CSP is a key control for PCI DSS 4.0 payment-page requirements. As enforcement gets stricter, inline scripts that used to work will be blocked.

RELATED GUIDEHow to stop spam and bot attacks on Adobe Commerce Cloud → Harden your Magento storeSecurity audits, patching and PCI-DSS 4.0 script controls.Get a free security audit →

The safer pattern

  • Return markup or JSON from AJAX endpoints — not <script> blocks
  • Initialise behaviour with data-mage-init or x-magento-init
  • Keep JavaScript in AMD modules
  • Use nonces only where unavoidable
  • Test with CSP in report-only mode first

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Waiting until after a breach to act
✕Restoring a backup without fixing the entry point
✕Leaving old plugins, extensions and admin users in place
✕Relying on a single tool instead of layered defences

CSP reports violations without blocking, so you can find issues safely.

title: Stop Spam & Bot Attacks on Adobe Commerce Cloud (2026 Guide) | VISIBI
description: Fake registrations, newsletter spam and card testing on Adobe Commerce Cloud — how to detect them and block them with Fastly WAF, reCAPTCHA and rate limits.
h1: How to stop spam and bot attacks on Adobe Commerce Cloud
html:
Home/Insights/Security
SECURITY

How to stop spam and bot attacks on Adobe Commerce Cloud

Fake registrations, newsletter spam and card testing on Adobe Commerce Cloud — how to detect them and block them with Fastly WAF, reCAPTCHA and rate limits.

By VISIBI Security team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·9 min read
QUICK ANSWER

Fake registrations, newsletter spam and card testing on Adobe Commerce Cloud — how to detect them and block them with Fastly WAF, reCAPTCHA and rate limits.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Most Adobe Commerce spam targets customer registration, newsletter, contact and checkout endpoints.
✓Adobe Commerce Cloud includes Fastly — use its WAF and rate limiting before adding plugins.
✓Enable Google reCAPTCHA v3 on every public form in the Magento admin.
✓Card-testing attacks need gateway-side rules too, not just front-end protection.

Signs your store is under a spam attack

Spam attacks rarely take a store offline, so they often go unnoticed until something else breaks — your email provider flags bounces, your payment gateway warns about declined transactions, or your CRM fills with gibberish accounts.

  • Hundreds of new customer accounts with random names or Cyrillic/Chinese characters
  • Newsletter sign-ups from disposable email domains
  • Spikes of $0–$1 authorisation attempts in your gateway (card testing)
  • Contact-form messages full of links
  • High traffic to /customer/account/createpost or /newsletter/subscriber/new
RELATED GUIDEWordPress security checklist: 15 steps to protect your site in 2026 →

Step 1: Turn on reCAPTCHA for every public form

Adobe Commerce ships with Google reCAPTCHA support. In the admin go to Stores → Configuration → Security → Google reCAPTCHA Storefront and enable reCAPTCHA v3 (invisible) for customer create, login, forgot password, newsletter, contact, product reviews, PayPal PayFlow and place order.

Use v3 “invisible” where you can — it scores traffic without showing a puzzle to real customers, so conversion is not affected.

Step 2: Use Fastly WAF and rate limiting

Every Adobe Commerce Cloud project includes Fastly CDN, and Pro plans include the Fastly Next-Gen WAF. Rules at the edge stop bots before they reach PHP, which also protects your server capacity during an attack.

  • Rate-limit POST requests to registration, newsletter and checkout endpoints
  • Block or challenge known bad ASNs and data-centre IP ranges
  • Use Fastly Edge ACLs to block repeat offenders
  • Add geo rules if you only sell in certain countries
Under attack right now?Our engineers can stop an active spam or card-testing attack on Adobe Commerce Cloud today.Get emergency help →

Step 3: Stop card testing at checkout

Card testing is the most expensive form of spam: fraudsters use your checkout to validate stolen cards, and your gateway may suspend your account. Combine platform and gateway defences.

  • Enable reCAPTCHA on “place order” and payment methods
  • Turn on your gateway’s fraud tools (Stripe Radar, Adyen RevenueProtect, Braintree Advanced Fraud)
  • Require a minimum order value for guest checkout during an attack
  • Alert on unusual numbers of failed payments per hour

Step 4: Clean up the damage

Once the attack is blocked, remove fake customers and subscribers so they don’t damage email deliverability or skew analytics. Export suspicious accounts by creation date and email domain, review, then delete in bulk. Re-check your email platform list and suppress disposable domains.

Step 5: Monitor so it doesn’t happen again

Set alerts for new-account spikes, failed payments and 4xx/5xx rates in New Relic (included with Adobe Commerce Cloud). Review Fastly WAF logs weekly for the first month after an attack.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Waiting until after a breach to act
✕Restoring a backup without fixing the entry point
✕Leaving old plugins, extensions and admin users in place
✕Relying on a single tool instead of layered defences

02Clean & patchEngineers remove threats and close the entry point.
03HardenWAF, 2FA, least privilege and platform hardening.

Does Adobe Commerce Cloud include a WAF?

Yes. Adobe Commerce Cloud Pro includes the Fastly Next-Gen WAF, and all Cloud projects include Fastly CDN with configurable rate limiting and edge ACLs.

Will reCAPTCHA hurt conversion?

reCAPTCHA v3 is invisible to most users and rarely affects conversion. Avoid v2 checkbox challenges on checkout.

How do I know if I am being card-tested?

Look for many small or failed authorisations from different cards in a short time, often with the same IP ranges or email patterns.

Home/Insights/Ecommerce
ECOMMERCE

Stop stock integrations triggering full Magento reindexing

Frequent ERP or stock-feed updates that call a full reindex create heavy CPU and database load. Process only changed SKUs and let Magento’s scheduled indexing do the rest.

By VISIBI Ecommerce team·Reviewed by Adnan Khan, Co-founder & CEO·Updated 29 September 2026·8 min read
QUICK ANSWER

Frequent ERP or stock-feed updates that call a full reindex create heavy CPU and database load. Process only changed SKUs and let Magento’s scheduled indexing do the rest.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

An external stock integration was updating inventory every few minutes and calling a full reindex each time. We changed it to detect differences first and let Magento’s scheduled indexing process only the changed records — removing a constant source of CPU and database load.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Calling reindexAll() on every stock sync is one of the most common causes of avoidable Magento load.
✓Most stock feeds contain thousands of rows but only a handful of real changes.
✓Diff first, write only what changed, and use “Update by Schedule” indexing.
BY THE NUMBERS
What changed after moving to diff-based updates
Thousandsrows received per feed run
A handfulrows actually changed
Partialindexing instead of full reindex
Typical pattern we see in stock integrations.

Why full reindexing hurts

A full reindex rebuilds index tables for the whole catalogue. Running it every few minutes competes with shoppers for CPU and database capacity — slowing category pages, search and checkout.

RELATED GUIDEGoogle Merchant Center feed optimisation: fix disapprovals and win more Shopping clicks → Need reliable ecommerce support?Patches, upgrades and fixes from certified developers.Get a free store health check →

The better pattern

  • Compare incoming stock with current values before writing
  • Update only SKUs whose quantity or status changed
  • Set indexers to “Update by Schedule” so Magento processes changelogs
  • Let cron and the mview queue apply partial reindexing
  • Log how many rows changed per run

What to measure

Track rows received vs rows changed, indexing time and database load before and after. The difference is usually dramatic.

Compute

  • Rightsize EC2 and RDS using Compute Optimizer recommendations

Storage

Networking and data transfer

NAT Gateway processing and cross-AZ traffic are common surprises. Use VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, keep chatty services in the same AZ where resilience allows, and serve static content through CloudFront.

FinOps habits

  • Set AWS Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection alerts
  • Review Cost Explorer monthly with engineering

Home/Insights/GEO & AI
GEO & AI

What is GEO? A plain-English guide to generative engine optimisation

GEO helps your brand get mentioned and cited in AI answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Perplexity. Here is how it works and how it differs from SEO.

By VISIBI AI team·Reviewed by Adnan Khan, Co-founder & CEO·Updated 29 September 2026·8 min read
QUICK ANSWER

GEO helps your brand get mentioned and cited in AI answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Perplexity. Here is how it works and how it differs from SEO.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓GEO means optimising so AI assistants mention, recommend and cite your brand.
✓AI answers draw on content that is clear, well-structured and widely corroborated.
✓Strong SEO is the foundation — GEO adds entity clarity, citations and answer-ready content.
STEP BY STEP
The GEO loop
1Audit AI answers for buyer prompts
2Fix entity facts & structured data
3Publish answer-first content
4Earn third-party citations
5Track share of voice monthly

What GEO actually is

Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) is the practice of improving how often — and how accurately — AI assistants mention your brand. When a buyer asks ChatGPT “best Magento agency in the UK”, the answer is generated from sources the model trusts. GEO is about becoming one of those sources.

RELATED GUIDEHow to get your business recommended by ChatGPT →

How AI chooses who to mention

  • Clear, consistent facts about who you are and what you do
  • Third-party corroboration: reviews, directories, press and comparison articles
  • Content that directly answers specific questions
  • Pages that are fast, crawlable and well-structured
  • Recency — updated content and active signals
Is AI recommending your competitors?Free AI visibility audit — see how ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity describe you.Get a free AI visibility audit →

GEO vs SEO

SEO wins clicks from search results; GEO wins mentions inside answers. They overlap heavily: technical health, helpful content and authority help both. GEO adds extra focus on entity consistency, quotable answers, structured data and being present on the sites AI models cite most.

Where to start

  • Ask AI tools the questions your buyers ask and record who is mentioned
  • Fix inconsistent company descriptions across your site and profiles
  • Create answer-first pages for your top 20 buyer questions
  • Earn mentions on trusted third-party sites in your niche
  • Track visibility monthly with a tool such as VISIBI Radar

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Treating AI visibility as a one-off project instead of a monthly habit
✕Describing your business differently on every profile and page
✕Publishing generic AI-written content with no first-hand expertise
✕Blocking AI crawlers by accident in robots.txt or firewall rules
HOW VISIBI CAN HELP

How we help with ai visibility & agents

01BenchmarkWe run your buyers’ real questions across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot.
02Fix the foundationsEntity facts, structured data and crawlability — fixed in code by our developers.
03Earn citationsAnswer-first content and third-party mentions on the sites AI trusts.
04Track & repeatMonthly share-of-voice reporting with VISIBI Radar.
Get a free AI visibility audit →Free · No obligation · Reply within 24 hours

Frequently asked questions

Is GEO replacing SEO?

No. AI assistants still rely on the open web, so SEO remains the foundation. GEO builds on it.

How long does GEO take?

Entity and content fixes can shift mentions within weeks; authority building compounds over months.

Can I measure GEO?

Yes — by tracking mention rate, citation rate and share of voice across a fixed set of prompts.

html:
Home/Insights/Ecommerce
ECOMMERCE

Why Magento shows the wrong stock: stale indexes explained

Products showing in or out of stock incorrectly? Direct inventory updates can leave stock index tables stale. Here is why it happens and how to fix it properly.

By VISIBI Ecommerce team·Reviewed by Adnan Khan, Co-founder & CEO·Updated 29 September 2026·7 min read
QUICK ANSWER

Products showing in or out of stock incorrectly? Direct inventory updates can leave stock index tables stale. Here is why it happens and how to fix it properly.

FROM OUR ENGINEERING WORKREAL CASE

We saw quantities updated correctly while the stock status index still held old values, so products appeared in or out of stock incorrectly until indexing caught up.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Magento reads stock status from index tables, not only the raw quantity.
✓Direct database updates can bypass the changelog, leaving indexes stale.
✓Healthy cron and correct update methods keep stock accurate.

How Magento decides stock status

The storefront relies on indexed stock status (for example cataloginventory_stock_status and inventory index tables). If quantities change without the index being updated, customers see old availability.

RELATED GUIDEGoogle Merchant Center feed optimisation: fix disapprovals and win more Shopping clicks → Need reliable ecommerce support?Patches, upgrades and fixes from certified developers.Get a free store health check →

Common causes

  • Integrations writing directly to stock tables
  • Indexers stuck or invalid
  • Cron not running or jobs failing
  • Cache not refreshed after updates
  • Multi-source inventory configuration issues

How to fix it

Update stock through Magento APIs or services, keep indexers on schedule with healthy cron, and monitor indexer status and backlog.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Choosing a platform on licence price instead of total cost of ownership
✕Launching a new site without an SEO redirect plan
✕Adding extensions and apps without checking performance or security
✕Leaving upgrades until peak season

Admin often reads raw data while the storefront uses indexed data.

As a one-off fix yes, but solve the root cause.

Home/Insights/Security
SECURITY

WordPress security checklist: 15 steps to protect your site in 2026

A practical WordPress and WooCommerce security checklist: updates, plugins, logins, file permissions, WAF, backups and monitoring.

By VISIBI Security team·Reviewed by Saeed Ak, Co-founder & CTO·Updated 29 September 2026·9 min read
QUICK ANSWER

A practical WordPress and WooCommerce security checklist: updates, plugins, logins, file permissions, WAF, backups and monitoring.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓Most WordPress hacks come from outdated or abandoned plugins.
✓Two-factor authentication and login limits stop most brute-force attacks.
✓A cloud WAF blocks attacks before they reach WordPress.
✓Tested off-site backups turn a disaster into a minor inconvenience.

Why WordPress sites get hacked

WordPress core is well maintained; most compromises come from vulnerable plugins and themes, weak passwords and poor hosting. Attackers use automated scanners, so small sites are targeted as often as big ones.

RELATED GUIDEHow to stop spam and bot attacks on Adobe Commerce Cloud →

The checklist

  • Keep WordPress core, themes and plugins updated (test on staging first)
  • Delete unused, abandoned and nulled plugins and themes
  • Enforce strong passwords and two-factor authentication for all admins
  • Limit login attempts and consider moving /wp-login.php
  • Disable XML-RPC if you don’t need it
  • Disable file editing in the dashboard (DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT)
  • Set correct file permissions (644 files, 755 folders, 600/640 wp-config.php)
  • Use unique salts and a non-default database prefix
  • Put the site behind a cloud WAF such as Cloudflare or Sucuri
  • Force HTTPS everywhere
  • Run daily off-site backups and test restores
  • Use PHP 8.2+ and a host that isolates sites
  • Give users the lowest role they need
  • Monitor file changes and uptime
  • Scan regularly for malware and blocklisting
Want this done for you?We harden WordPress and WooCommerce and keep them patched every month.Get a free WordPress security scan →

Extra steps for WooCommerce

Online stores are a bigger target. Protect checkout from card testing with reCAPTCHA and gateway fraud tools, block fake account registrations, and keep payment plugins updated immediately when security releases appear.

What to do if you are hacked

Put the site into maintenance mode, change all passwords, restore a clean backup or have the infection professionally removed, then patch whatever let the attacker in. Request a review in Google Search Console if you were flagged.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Waiting until after a breach to act
✕Restoring a backup without fixing the entry point
✕Leaving old plugins, extensions and admin users in place
✕Relying on a single tool instead of layered defences

Is a security plugin enough?

It helps, but updates, hardening, backups and a cloud WAF stop far more attacks than a plugin alone.

How often should I update WordPress?

Apply security updates as soon as possible; test feature updates on staging weekly or fortnightly.

Is WordPress secure for ecommerce?

Yes, when properly hardened, hosted and maintained.

h1: llms.txt explained: should your website have one?
html:
Home/Insights/GEO & AI
GEO & AI

llms.txt explained: should your website have one?

llms.txt is a proposed file that gives AI tools a clean summary of your site. What it is, how to create one, and whether it helps AI visibility.

By VISIBI AI team·Reviewed by Adnan Khan, Co-founder & CEO·Updated 29 September 2026·6 min read
QUICK ANSWER

llms.txt is a proposed file that gives AI tools a clean summary of your site. What it is, how to create one, and whether it helps AI visibility.

KEY TAKEAWAYS
✓llms.txt is a proposed markdown file at your site root that summarises key pages for AI tools.
✓It is not an official standard and major AI platforms have not confirmed they rely on it.
✓It is cheap to add — but fundamentals like crawlability and clear content matter far more.

What llms.txt is

llms.txt is a community proposal: a plain markdown file at yourdomain.com/llms.txt that lists your most important pages with short descriptions, making it easier for AI tools to understand your site without parsing complex HTML.

RELATED GUIDEWhat is GEO? A plain-English guide to generative engine optimisation →

What to include

  • A one-line description of your business
  • Links to key service, product and pricing pages
  • Links to documentation, FAQs and policies
  • Short descriptions for each link
Is AI recommending your competitors?Free AI visibility audit — see how ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity describe you.Get a free AI visibility audit →

Does it help AI visibility?

Evidence is limited. Treat it as a low-effort extra rather than a strategy. The things that clearly matter are crawlable pages, consistent facts, strong content and third-party mentions.

Don’t block AI crawlers by accident

Check robots.txt and your CDN or firewall rules. Some security settings block AI crawlers such as GPTBot or PerplexityBot, which can stop your content being used in answers.

Common mistakes to avoid

✕Treating AI visibility as a one-off project instead of a monthly habit
✕Describing your business differently on every profile and page
✕Publishing generic AI-written content with no first-hand expertise
✕Blocking AI crawlers by accident in robots.txt or firewall rules
HOW VISIBI CAN HELP

How we help with ai visibility & agents

Is llms.txt the same as robots.txt?

No. robots.txt controls crawling; llms.txt is a proposed summary for AI tools.

Will Google use llms.txt?

Google has not said it uses llms.txt for search or AI Overviews.

How long does it take to create?

Usually under an hour for a small site.

LEGAL

Privacy & cookie policy

Last updated: 28 September 2026

TEMPLATE · HAVE A SOLICITOR REVIEW BEFORE PUBLISHING

1. Who we are

VISIBI (“we”, “us”) provides AI visibility, ecommerce, cloud, security and marketing services and the VISIBI Radar software, serving clients in the United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates and United States. We are the data controller for personal data collected through this website. Contact: privacy@govisibi.ai.

2. What we collect

  • Contact details you give us in forms (name, email, company, website URL, phone).
  • Meeting and enquiry details (preferred time, location, project information).
  • Account and usage data if you sign up for VISIBI Radar.
  • Technical data such as IP address, browser and pages visited, collected via cookies with your consent.

3. How and why we use it

  • To reply to enquiries, arrange meetings and provide quotes (legitimate interests / steps before a contract).
  • To deliver services and software you buy from us (contract).
  • To send marketing emails where you have opted in (consent — you can unsubscribe any time).
  • To measure and improve the website (consent for analytics cookies).
  • To meet legal, tax and accounting obligations (legal obligation).

4. Sharing and international transfers

We share data only with trusted processors who help us run our business (for example hosting, email, CRM and analytics providers), under contracts that protect your data. Where data moves between the UK, UAE, EEA or other countries, we use appropriate safeguards such as the UK International Data Transfer Agreement or Standard Contractual Clauses. We never sell your personal data.

5. How long we keep it

Enquiry data is kept for up to 24 months after our last contact. Client and account records are kept for the length of the relationship plus 6 years for legal and tax purposes.

6. Your rights

Under UK GDPR and the UAE Personal Data Protection Law you can ask to access, correct, delete, restrict or port your data, and object to processing or withdraw consent. Email privacy@govisibi.ai. In the UK you can also complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ico.org.uk).

7. Cookies

We use strictly necessary cookies to run the site. With your consent we also use analytics cookies (such as Google Analytics 4) and advertising cookies (such as Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, Meta and LinkedIn) to measure and improve our marketing. We use Google Consent Mode, so these tags respect your choice. You can change your preferences at any time via the cookie banner or your browser settings.
